title: subject_srv.exe Installed as Persistent Auto-Start Service (F-Response Subject)
observation: EID 7045 at 2018-09-06T19:25:36Z on base-file.shieldbase.lan: service "F-Response Subject" installed with StartType=auto start, AccountName=LocalSystem, executable C:\windows\subject_srv.exe, installed by SID S-1-5-21-3445421715-2530590580-3149308974-1185 (non-SYSTEM domain account). EID 4688 at same second confirms process creation at PID 0x1810 (parent PID 0x218). Path is anomalous — C:\windows\ not C:\Windows\System32\.
interpretation: A domain user (SID -1185) installed subject_srv.exe as a LocalSystem auto-start service. The non-standard path (C:\windows\ vs System32) and the use of a domain account (not SYSTEM) to register a LocalSystem service are red flags. F-Response is a legitimate DFIR tool for live forensic acquisition; its presence here is consistent with attacker or unauthorised responder lateral tool deployment.

title: subject_srv.exe Timestomped — $SI Modified Backdated with Zero Microseconds
observation: MFT pre-existing CSV (entry 123285, .\Windows\subject_srv.exe): $SI Modified (LastModified0x10) = 2018-04-10 19:29:48.0000000 (zero microseconds, rounded to second) while $FN Modified (LastModified0x30) = 2018-09-06 19:25:36.5115342. The uSecZeros flag is True. Copied flag is True. $SI Created and $FN Created both show 2018-09-06, so only the Modified timestamp was backdated approximately 5 months. SHA1 in Amcache pre-existing CSV: 6935db820d990060446e836c2027fc2adfd9099e.
interpretation: The $SI Modified timestamp was deliberately altered to appear as if the file was last modified in April 2018 — approximately 5 months before actual placement (September 2018). The .000 microsecond precision and $SI/$FN mismatch are classic timestomping signatures. This is anti-forensic tradecraft to evade timeline-based detection. The Copied=True flag indicates the file was transferred cross-volume (consistent with lateral tool deployment).
artifact_source: MFT pre-existing CSV (analysis/mft_out/mft) entry 123285; Amcache pre-existing CSV (analysis/amcache_out/Amcache_UnassociatedFileEntries)

title: Suspicious Auto-Start Services — "Microsoft Advanced API 64/32" — Possible Malware Phase 1
observation: EID 7045 at 2018-04-26T01:13:12Z: service "Microsoft Advanced API 64" installed auto-start, LocalSystem, executable C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Advanced API 64\msadvapi2_64.exe. EID 7045 at 2018-04-26T01:13:36Z: service "Microsoft Advanced API 32" installed auto-start, LocalSystem, executable C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Advanced API 32\msadvapi2_32.exe. Both installed by SID S-1-5-18 (SYSTEM). Time of installation is 01:13 UTC (off-hours).
interpretation: These services use plausible-sounding names mimicking Windows API infrastructure but are not legitimate Microsoft services (no real Windows service by this name exists). The 64-bit binary installed under Program Files (x86) is anomalous. Off-hours installation by SYSTEM suggests automated deployment. These may represent the initial persistence implant dropped during the April 2018 compromise phase — approximately 5 months before the September 2018 subject_srv.exe deployment. Corroboration via Amcache hash lookup is blocked by hive incompatibility.
